title: Seven full uncompressed backup copies will fill the free Cloudflare store, and the backup then stops
what: Every night the whole database, every row of every table, is copied as plain text and kept for 7 days in the Cloudflare key store, with no squeezing. Member photos are written as long text that is about twice their real size. The free Cloudflare plan gives 1 GB in that store for the whole account. Once one copy is about 140 MB, seven copies fill it, new copies cannot be saved, and the nightly backup fails. Nothing warns before that point. The outage watch only notices after a night's backup is already missing. Each copy also leaves the gym server as download traffic every night, and that traffic is not watched either.
expected: Backup copies are made smaller before they are stored, their total size is checked against the store's limit, and MettleUp is warned well before the store is full.
who: MettleUp, and every gym if a restore is ever needed
how_often: every night, getting worse as data grows
fix_line: Squeeze each copy before storing it, keep fewer full copies, and warn when the store passes a set share of its limit

title: Every door-machine punch is kept on the gym server for ever
what: When the entry machines are switched on, every punch at the gym door is saved as one row. Other lists in this part (leaderboard days, gym mate workouts, busy times, push jobs) delete old rows after 30 to 90 days, but door punches are never deleted. A gym with 300 visits a day adds about 15 MB a year. Thirty such gyms add about 450 MB a year, close to the free 500 MB that all gyms share. When the database is full, saving members and payments stops for every gym.
expected: Old door punches are deleted after a set time (for example 90 days), since each visit is already kept in the gym's own records.
who: every gym once entry machines are on
how_often: grows every day a machine is used
fix_line: Delete door punches older than a set number of days, the way other lists already do

title: On a busy day gym-message pop-ups over 6 hours late are quietly dropped, and nobody is told
what: The free Cloudflare plan lets the sender make about 45 outside calls a minute, so about 2,700 phone pop-ups go out an hour across all gyms. A message to everyone at a large gym can be sent to up to 5,000 people. When many gyms send in the same morning, the line of pop-ups grows. Any message still waiting after 6 hours is marked late and skipped. Nothing reads those late marks, so MettleUp never learns that members missed pop-ups. Members still see the message inside the app later.
expected: MettleUp is warned when pop-ups start to back up or are skipped as late, before the 6-hour cut-off is reached.
who: gym members and owners on busy days
how_often: only when many gyms send at once
fix_line: Count pop-ups waiting and skipped as late, and warn MettleUp when either passes a set number
